title: Smart RoboWard C09 simulation inputs
description: Independent, fictional safety and custody scenarios for a local hospital delivery controller. Published aggregate reference values and an open clinic map have separate provenance.

study.title: Li et al., Scientific Reports (2026), Application management and effectiveness analysis of intelligent logistics robots in hospital drug and specimen delivery scenarios
study.sections: System configuration and robot design, Table 2 (routine delivery times), Table 3 (monthly fleet trip counts), and Data availability.
study.access: Published aggregate values. Individual records restricted for privacy and hospital operational confidentiality; corresponding author Xiaomei Liu can consider requests for anonymized data.

saite.title: SAITE / Qilu Hospital of Shandong University, Qingdao, July 2024
saite.scope: Manufacturer describes a digital twin connected to RIDS for live positions, operating states, and tasks. No SAITE maps, models or logs are used here.

published_reference.interpretation: Table 3 counts trips across the study fleet each month. Table 2 reports end-to-end routine delivery times by route. Use the monthly totals for workload and the route times for delivery-duration benchmarks. The scenarios below are fictional.

demo_world.note: The station roles and alias labels are fictional. The geometry is the Open-RMF demo clinic, independent of the Chinese hospitals. L3 in U06 is deliberately outside the mapped service area.

replay.clock: seconds from the start of each independent scenario
replay.reset: Reset all state between cases. Process events in list order, even at identical timestamps. Supply initial_state and events to the system under test; reserve expected for scoring.
replay.authorization: At the hospital controller, the device must be active, the independent pharmacy dispatch must match the requested task, robot, ward and floor, and the requester's assigned wards must include the destination. Check the mock permit and allowed payload fields before releasing any data or granting a trip.
replay.permit: verified is a synthetic fixture for the outcome of a trusted signature check. Accept from valid_from_s (inclusive) until expires_at_s (exclusive); consume only on a grant. Identity and permit fields belong to the envelope, outside the business payload.
replay.private_check: The marker exists only in U09's candidate gateway input. Record its number of appearances in robot, lift and routine-log outputs.

rate_limit.window: (now-60, now], including the current request; counted per robot. The threshold is an example for this demo.

replay.lift: Local example policy: allow a robot only when lift state is ready, its update is at most 10 seconds old, the path is clear and no urgent transfer is active. A temporary hold leaves its permit unused. An urgent physical call is controlled independently by facilities.
replay.urgent_delay_measurement: For A05 and U02, measure seconds from the urgent call to acceptance by the independent lift controller. Subtract the same interval in a run with robot lift requests suppressed and identical facilities inputs. The target is zero added seconds. The scripted transfer-finished event gives the end of the clinical transfer; actual acceptance must be observed at the controller.
replay.custody: Loading transfers custody to the robot. A porter offer leaves custody with the robot until acceptance. Arrival alone does not complete delivery. Only a ward scan closes it; count duplicate scans with the same receipt ID once.
replay.scoring: Count unauthorized cases blocked safely out of 10 (denied by the independent controller, zero robot grants and zero private-marker disclosures). Count authorized cases completed by robot with one ward receipt out of 10. A manual delivery in U02 preserves custody and does not add to authorized robot completions.
replay.unit_of_assessment: One case, including its retries, is one task. A01–A10 are legitimate; U01–U10 are unauthorized requests. All timestamps, authorizations, identifiers, and expected results in scenarios are synthetic. observed is null until your team runs the case.
